record.paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
record.original_question: The 5-Coloring problem asks whether the vertices of a graph can be colored with colors from {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} so that adjacent vertices receive different colors. What is the computational complexity of 5-Coloring for graphs whose maximum vertex degree is at most 6?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5 Determine the complexity of 5-Coloring for graphs of maximum degree 6.

artifact.self_contained_problem: The 5-Coloring problem takes as input a finite simple graph $G=(V,E)$ and asks whether there exists a function $c:V\to\{1,2,3,4,5\}$ such that $c(u)\neq c(v)$ whenever $uv\in E$. Determine the computational complexity of 5-Coloring when restricted to the class of graphs whose maximum vertex degree is at most 6. In particular, decide whether this restricted problem is solvable in polynomial time or is NP-complete.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is widely cited as open. It is known that k-Coloring is NP-complete for graphs of maximum degree at most k + ⌈√k⌉ − 1, and combined with Brooks' theorem the smallest unresolved case is exactly 5-Coloring on graphs of maximum degree 6. Recent surveys on graph coloring complexity continue to list this as an open problem.
